claim: Antibodies play a central role in the adaptive immune system and in biotechnology.
source: Despite the central role that antibodies play in the adaptive immune system and in biotechnology, much remains unknown about the quantitative relationship between an antibody's amino acid sequence and its antigen binding affinity.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in immunology and biotechnology, representing scientific consensus.

claim: Much remains unknown about the quantitative relationship between an antibody's amino acid sequence and its antigen binding affinity.
source: Despite the central role that antibodies play in the adaptive immune system and in biotechnology, much remains unknown about the quantitative relationship between an antibody's amino acid sequence and its antigen binding affinity.
evidence: This statement reflects the current state of knowledge in the field and motivates the study.

claim: Tite-Seq is capable of measuring binding titration curves and corresponding affinities for thousands of variant antibodies in parallel.
source: Here we describe a new experimental approach, called Tite-Seq, that is capable of measuring binding titration curves and corresponding affinities for thousands of variant antibodies in parallel.
evidence: This is the primary claim of the paper, supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The measurement of titration curves eliminates the confounding effects of antibody expression and stability that arise in standard deep mutational scanning assays.
source: The measurement of titration curves eliminates the confounding effects of antibody expression and stability that arise in standard deep mutational scanning assays.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental design and data analysis presented in the paper, particularly in Figure 4—figure supplement 5 and Figure 4—figure supplement 6.

claim: Tite-Seq was demonstrated on the CDR1H and CDR3H regions of a well-studied scFv antibody.
source: We demonstrate Tite-Seq on the CDR1H and CDR3H regions of a well-studied scFv antibody.
evidence: This is directly supported by the experimental data presented in the Results section.

claim: The Tite-Seq data shed light on the structural basis for antigen binding affinity.
source: Our data shed light on the structural basis for antigen binding affinity and suggests a role for secondary CDR loops in establishing antibody stability.
evidence: This is supported by the structural analysis presented in Figure 6.

claim: The Tite-Seq data suggest a role for secondary CDR loops in establishing antibody stability.
source: Our data shed light on the structural basis for antigen binding affinity and suggests a role for secondary CDR loops in establishing antibody stability.
evidence: This is inferred from the expression data presented in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Tite-Seq fills a large gap in the ability to measure critical aspects of the adaptive immune system.
source: Tite-Seq fills a large gap in the ability to measure critical aspects of the adaptive immune system, and can be readily used for studying sequence-affinity landscapes in other protein systems.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about the potential impact of the method.

claim: Tite-Seq can be readily used for studying sequence-affinity landscapes in other protein systems.
source: Tite-Seq fills a large gap in the ability to measure critical aspects of the adaptive immune system, and can be readily used for studying sequence-affinity landscapes in other protein systems.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about the generalizability of the method.

claim: B-cells contribute to immune defense by producing antibodies that bind specifically to foreign antigens.
source: B-cells contribute to immune defense by producing antibodies, proteins that bind specifically to foreign antigens.
evidence: This is established knowledge in immunology.

claim: The astonishing capability of antibodies to recognize virtually any foreign molecule has been repurposed by scientists in a wide variety of experimental techniques.
source: The astonishing capability of antibodies to recognize virtually any foreign molecule has been repurposed by scientists in a wide variety of experimental techniques (immunofluorescence, western blots, ELISA, ChIP-Seq, etc.).
evidence: This is established knowledge in biotechnology and molecular biology.

claim: Antibody-based therapeutic drugs have been developed for treating many different diseases, including cancer.
source: Antibody-based therapeutic drugs have also been developed for treating many different diseases, including cancer (Chan and Carter, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: The antigenic specificity of antibodies in humans, mice, and most jawed vertebrates is primarily governed by six complementarity determining regions (CDRs), each roughly 10 amino acids long.
source: The antigenic specificity of antibodies in humans, mice, and most jawed vertebrates is primarily governed by six complementarity determining regions (CDRs), each roughly 10 amino acids (aa) long.
evidence: This is established knowledge in immunology.

claim: Three CDRs (denoted CDR1H, CDR2H, and CDR3H) are located on the antibody heavy chain, and three are on the light chain.
source: Three CDRs (denoted CDR1H, CDR2H, and CDR3H) are located on the antibody heavy chain, and three are on the light chain.
evidence: This is established knowledge in immunology.

claim: During B-cell differentiation, the six CDR sequences are randomized through V(D)J recombination, then selected for functionality as well as against the ability to recognize host antigens.
source: During B-cell differentiation, these six sequences are randomized through V(D)J recombination, then selected for functionality as well as against the ability to recognize host antigens.
evidence: This is established knowledge in immunology.

claim: Upon participation in an immune response, CDR regions can further undergo somatic hypermutation and selection, yielding higher-affinity antibodies for specific antigens.
source: Upon participation in an immune response, CDR regions can further undergo somatic hypermutation and selection, yielding higher-affinity antibodies for specific antigens.
evidence: This is established knowledge in immunology.

claim: Among the CDRs, CDR3H is the most highly variable and typically contributes the most to antigen specificity.
source: Among the CDRs, CDR3H is the most highly variable and typically contributes the most to antigen specificity; less clear are the functional roles of the other CDRs, which often do not interact with the target antigen directly.
evidence: This is established knowledge in immunology.

claim: The functional roles of CDRs other than CDR3H are less clear, as they often do not interact with the target antigen directly.
source: Among the CDRs, CDR3H is the most highly variable and typically contributes the most to antigen specificity; less clear are the functional roles of the other CDRs, which often do not interact with the target antigen directly.
evidence: This is established knowledge in immunology and motivates the investigation in this study.

claim: Many high-throughput techniques have been developed for optimizing antibodies ex vivo, including phage display, ribosome display, yeast display, and mammalian cell display.
source: Many high-throughput techniques, including phage display (Smith, 1985; Vaughan et al., 1996; Schirrmann et al., 2011), ribosome display (Fujino et al., 2012), yeast display (Boder and Wittrup, 1997; Gai and Wittrup, 2007), and mammalian cell display (Forsyth et al., 2013), have been developed for optimizing antibodies ex vivo.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to the literature.

claim: Advances in DNA sequencing technology have made it possible to effectively monitor both antibody and T-cell receptor diversity within immune repertoires.
source: Advances in DNA sequencing technology have also made it possible to effectively monitor both antibody and T-cell receptor diversity within immune repertoires, e.g. in healthy individuals (Boyd et al., 2009; Weinstein et al., 2009; Robins et al., 2009, 2010; Mora et al., 2010; Venturi et al., 2011; Murugan et al., 2012; Zvyagin et al., 2014; Elhanati et al., 2014; Qi et al., 2014; Thomas et al., 2014; Elhanati et al., 2015), in specific tissues (Madi et al., 2014), in individuals with diseases (Parameswaran et al., 2013) or following vaccination (Jiang et al., 2013; Vollmers et al., 2013; Laserson et al., 2014; Galson et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to the literature.

claim: Deep mutational scanning (DMS) assays provide one potential method for measuring binding affinities with high enough throughput to effectively explore antibody sequence-affinity landscapes.
source: Recently developed 'deep mutational scanning' (DMS) assays (Fowler and Fields, 2014) provide one potential method for measuring binding affinities with high enough throughput to effectively explore antibody sequence-affinity landscapes.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature and represents the motivation for developing Tite-Seq.

claim: In DMS experiments, one begins with a library of variants of a specific protein, enriches proteins with high levels of a particular activity, and scores sequences according to enrichment.
source: In DMS experiments, one begins with a library of variants of a specific protein. Proteins that have high levels of a particular activity of interest are then enriched via one or more rounds of selection, which can be carried out in a variety of ways. The set of enriched sequences is then compared to the initial library, and protein sequences (or mutations within these sequences) are scored according to how much this enrichment procedure increases their prevalence.
evidence: This is a description of established DMS methodology.

claim: No DMS assay has yet been shown to provide absolute quantitative binding affinity measurements (dissociation constants in molar units).
source: But no DMS assay has yet been shown to provide absolute quantitative binding affinity measurements, i.e., dissociation constants in molar units.
evidence: This is a claim about the state of the field prior to this work, supported by the discussion of previous methods.

claim: One of the first DMS experiments used phage display technology to measure how mutations in a WW domain affect the affinity of this domain for its peptide ligand, but did not yield quantitative affinities.
source: For example, one of the first DMS experiments (Fowler et al., 2010) used phage display technology to measure how mutations in a WW domain affect the affinity of this domain for its peptide ligand. These data were sufficient to compute enrichment ratios and corresponding sequence logos, but they did not yield quantitative affinities.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Analogous DMS experiments have been performed on antibodies using yeast display and mammalian cell display.
source: Analogous experiments have since been performed on antibodies using yeast display (Reich et al., 2015; Kowalsky et al., 2015) and mammalian cell display (Forsyth et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Yeast-display-based DMS assays have proven particularly useful for mapping protein epitopes that are targeted by specific antibodies of interest.
source: Yeast-display-based DMS assays have also proven particularly useful for mapping protein epitopes that are targeted by specific antibodies of interest (Kowalsky et al., 2015; Doolan and Colby, 2015; Van Blarcom et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: None of the previous DMS approaches provides quantitative affinity values.
source: Still, none of these approaches provides quantitative affinity values.
evidence: This is a claim about the limitations of previous methods, supported by the discussion of those methods.

claim: SORTCERY is a DMS assay that combines yeast display and quantitative modeling and has been shown to provide approximate rank-order values for the affinity of a specific protein for short unstructured peptides of varying sequence.
source: SORTCERY (Reich et al., 2015, ), a DMS assay that combines yeast display and quantitative modeling, has been shown to provide approximate rank-order values for the affinity of a specific protein for short unstructured peptides of varying sequence.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Determining quantitative affinities from SORTCERY data requires separate low-throughput calibration measurements.
source: Determining quantitative affinities from SORTCERY data, however, requires separate low-throughput calibration measurements (Reich et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: It is unclear how well SORTCERY, if applied to a library of folded proteins rather than unstructured peptides, can distinguish sequence-dependence effects on affinity from sequence-dependent effects on protein expression and stability.
source: Moreover, it is unclear how well SORTCERY, if applied to a library of folded proteins rather than unstructured peptides, can distinguish sequence-dependence effects on affinity from sequence-dependent effects on protein expression and stability.
evidence: This is an inference about the limitations of SORTCERY based on its design.

claim: A DMS assay based on yeast display has been described for measuring fold-changes in affinity relative to a reference protein, but does not provide absolute values for dissociation constants, is vulnerable to confounding effects, and has only a 10-fold dynamic range.
source: Other recent work has described a DMS assay, again based on yeast display, for measuring fold-changes in affinity relative to a reference protein (Kowalsky and Whitehead, 2016). This method, however, does not provide absolute values for dissociation constants, is vulnerable to the confounding effects of sequence-dependent expression and protein stability, and was observed to have only a 10-fold dynamic range.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Tite-Seq builds on the capabilities of Sort-Seq, an experimental strategy that was first developed for studying transcriptional regulatory sequences in bacteria.
source: Tite-Seq, like SORTCERY, builds on the capabilities of Sort-Seq, an experimental strategy that was first developed for studying transcriptional regulatory sequences in bacteria (Kinney et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Sort-Seq combines fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) with high-throughput sequencing to provide massively parallel measurements of cellular fluorescence.
source: Sort-Seq combines fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) with high-throughput sequencing to provide massively parallel measurements of cellular fluorescence.
evidence: This is a description of the Sort-Seq method, supported by a citation.

claim: In the Tite-Seq assay, Sort-Seq is applied to antibodies displayed on the surface of yeast cells and incubated with antigen at a wide range of concentrations.
source: In the Tite-Seq assay, Sort-Seq is applied to antibodies displayed on the surface of yeast cells and incubated with antigen at a wide range of concentrations.
evidence: This is a description of the Tite-Seq method, supported by the experimental data.

claim: The affinity values provided by Tite-Seq are not confounded by the effect that sequence variation can have on the amount of protein expressed on the surface of cells or the specific activity of displayed proteins.
source: Moreover, the resulting affinity values provided by Tite-Seq are not confounded by the (rather substantial) effect that sequence variation can have on either (a) the amount of protein expressed on the surface of cells or (b) the specific activity of displayed proteins (i.e., the fraction of protein molecules that are functional).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental design and data analysis, particularly Figure 4—figure supplement 5 and Figure 4—figure supplement 6.

claim: Tite-Seq was demonstrated on a protein library derived from a well-studied single-chain variable fragment (scFv) antibody specific to the small molecule fluorescein.
source: We demonstrated Tite-Seq on a protein library derived from a well-studied single-chain variable fragment (scFv) antibody specific to the small molecule fluorescein (Boder and Wittrup, 1997; Boder et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data and citations to the literature.

claim: Mutations in the Tite-Seq library were restricted to CDR1H and CDR3H regions, which are known to play an important role in the antigen recognition of this scFv.
source: Mutations were restricted to CDR1H and CDR3H regions, which are known to play an important role in the antigen recognition of this scFv (Boder et al., 2000; Midelfort et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The Tite-Seq affinity measurements were validated with binding curves for a handful of clones measured using standard low-throughput flow cytometry.
source: The resulting affinity measurements were validated with binding curves for a handful of clones measured using standard low-throughput flow cytometry.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data presented in Figure 4.

claim: The Tite-Seq measurements reveal both expected and unexpected differences between the effects of mutations in CDR1H and CDR3H.
source: Our Tite-Seq measurements reveal both expected and unexpected differences between the effects of mutations in CDR1H and CDR3H.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data presented in Figure 5.

claim: The Tite-Seq data shed light on structural aspects of antigen recognition that are independent of effects on antibody stability.
source: These data also shed light on structural aspects of antigen recognition that are independent of effects on antibody stability.
evidence: This is supported by the structural analysis presented in Figure 6.

claim: In Tite-Seq, a library of variant antibodies is displayed on the surface of yeast cells such that each cell displays a single antibody variant, and each variant is expressed on the surface of multiple cells.
source: First, a library of variant antibodies is displayed on the surface of yeast cells (Figure 1A). The composition of this library is such that each cell displays a single antibody variant, and each variant is expressed on the surface of multiple cells.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design, illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: In Tite-Seq, cells are incubated with the antigen of interest, bound antigen is fluorescently labeled, and FACS is used to sort cells into multiple bins based on fluorescent readout.
source: Cells are then incubated with the antigen of interest, bound antigen is fluorescently labeled, and fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) is used to sort cells one-by-one into multiple 'bins' based on this fluorescent readout (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design, illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: In Tite-Seq, deep sequencing is used to survey the antibody variants present in each bin.
source: Deep sequencing is then used to survey the antibody variants present in each bin.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: In Tite-Seq, each variant antibody is sorted multiple times and will be associated with a histogram of counts spread across one or more bins.
source: Because each variant antibody is sorted multiple times, it will be associated with a histogram of counts spread across one or more bins (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design, illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: The spread in each histogram in Tite-Seq is due to cell-to-cell variability in antibody expression and to the inherent noisiness of flow cytometry measurements.
source: The spread in each histogram is due to cell-to-cell variability in antibody expression, and to the inherent noisiness of flow cytometry measurements.
evidence: This is an inference about the sources of experimental noise.

claim: In Tite-Seq, the histogram corresponding to each antibody variant is used to compute an 'average bin number', which serves as a proxy measurement for the average amount of bound antigen per cell.
source: Finally, the histogram corresponding to each antibody variant is used to compute an 'average bin number' (Figure 1C, dots), which serves as a proxy measurement for the average amount of bound antigen per cell.
evidence: This is a description of the data analysis procedure, illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: Standard flow cytometry measurements of binding curves can only be performed in a low-throughput manner.
source: Such measurements, however, can only be performed in a low-throughput manner.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of standard methods.

claim: Tite-Seq allows thousands of binding titration curves to be measured in parallel.
source: Tite-Seq allows thousands of binding titration curves to be measured in parallel.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data presented in the Results section.

claim: In Tite-Seq, the Sort-Seq procedure is performed at multiple antigen concentrations, and the resulting average bin number for each variant antibody is plotted against concentration.
source: The Sort-Seq procedure illustrated in Figure 1A–C is performed at multiple antigen concentrations, and the resulting average bin number for each variant antibody is plotted against concentration.
evidence: This is a description of the Tite-Seq procedure.

claim: Sort-Seq experiments used to measure sequence-affinity landscapes must be carried out over a range of concentrations large enough to encompass the variation in KD.
source: Sort-Seq experiments used to measure sequence-affinity landscapes must therefore be carried out over a range of concentrations large enough to encompass this variation.
evidence: This is an inference about the experimental design requirements.

claim: Different antibody variants often lead to different levels of functional antibody expression on the yeast cell surface.
source: Furthermore, as illustrated in Figure 1C and D, different antibody variants often lead to different levels of functional antibody expression on the yeast cell surface.
evidence: This is illustrated in Figure 1C and D.

claim: Only by measuring full titration curves can the effect that sequence has on affinity be deconvolved from sequence-dependent effects on functional protein expression.
source: Only by measuring full titration curves can the effect that sequence has on affinity be deconvolved from sequence-dependent effects on functional protein expression.
evidence: This is an inference about the advantages of the Tite-Seq approach.

claim: The 4-4-20 single chain variable fragment (scFv) antibody binds the small molecule fluorescein with KD = 1.2 nM.
source: To test the feasibility of Tite-Seq, we used a well-characterized antibody-antigen system: the 4-4-20 single chain variable fragment (scFv) antibody (Boder and Wittrup, 1997), which binds the small molecule fluorescein with KD=1.2 nM (Gai and Wittrup, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: The 4-4-20 antibody-antigen system was used in early work to establish the capabilities of yeast display.
source: This system was used in early work to establish the capabilities of yeast display (Boder and Wittrup, 1997), and a high resolution co-crystal structure of the 4-4-20 antibody bound to fluorescein, shown in Figure 2A, has been determined (Whitlow et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: A high resolution co-crystal structure of the 4-4-20 antibody bound to fluorescein has been determined.
source: This system was used in early work to establish the capabilities of yeast display (Boder and Wittrup, 1997), and a high resolution co-crystal structure of the 4-4-20 antibody bound to fluorescein, shown in Figure 2A, has been determined (Whitlow et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: An ultra-high-affinity (KD = 270 fM) variant of the 4-4-20 scFv, called 4m5.3, has been found.
source: An ultra-high-affinity (KD=270 fM) variant of this scFv, called 4m5.3, has also been found (Boder et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: The 1H library consisted of all 600 single-codon variants of a 10 aa region encompassing CDR1H, 1100 randomly chosen 2-codon variants, and 150 random 3-codon variants.
source: The resulting 1H library consisted of all 600 single-codon variants of this 10 aa region, 1100 randomly chosen 2-codon variants, and 150 random 3-codon variants (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a description of the library composition, shown in Figure 2D.

claim: An analogous 3H library was generated for a 10 aa region containing the CDR3H region of the scFv.
source: An analogous '3H' library was generated for a 10 aa region containing the CDR3H region of this scFv.
evidence: This is a description of the library composition.

claim: Tite-Seq was carried out by incubating yeast cells expressing scFv from the mixed library with fluorescein-biotin at one of eleven concentrations: 0 M, 10^-9.5 M, 10^-9 M, 10^-8.5 M, 10^-8 M, 10^-7.5 M, 10^-7 M, 10^-6.5 M, 10^-6 M, 10^-5.5 M, and 10^-5 M.
source: Tite-Seq was carried out as follows. Yeast cells expressing scFv from the mixed library were incubated with fluorescein-biotin at one of eleven concentrations: 0 M, 10-9.5 M, 10-9 M, 10-8.5 M, 10-8 M, 10-7.5 M, 10-7 M, 10-6.5 M, 10-6 M, 10-5.5 M, and 10-5 M.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental procedure.

claim: After PE labeling of bound antigen, cells were sorted into four bins using FACS.
source: After subsequent PE labeling of bound antigen, cells were sorted into four bins using FACS (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental procedure, shown in Figure 3A.

claim: BV-labeled cells were sorted according to measured scFv expression levels.
source: Separately, BV-labeled cells were sorted according to measured scFv expression levels (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental procedure, shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Each bin of cells was regrown and bulk DNA was extracted.
source: Each bin of cells was regrown and bulk DNA was extracted.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental procedure.

claim: The 1H and 3H variable regions were PCR amplified and sequenced using paired-end Illumina sequencing.
source: The 1H and 3H variable regions were then PCR amplified and sequenced using paired-end Illumina sequencing, as described in Appendix 4.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental procedure.

claim: The final Tite-Seq data set consisted of an average of 2.6×10^6 sequences per bin across all 48 bins.
source: The final data set consisted of an average of 2.6×106 sequences per bin across all 48 bins (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a description of the data obtained, shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Three independent replicates of the Tite-Seq experiment were performed on three different days.
source: Three independent replicates of this experiment were performed on three different days.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: For each variant scFv gene, a KD value was inferred by fitting a binding curve to the resulting Tite-Seq data, with separate curves independently fit to data from each Tite-Seq experiment.
source: For each variant scFv gene, a KD value was inferred by fitting a binding curve to the resulting Tite-Seq data, with separate curves independently fit to data from each Tite-Seq experiment (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a description of the data analysis procedure, illustrated in Figure 4A.

claim: The Tite-Seq fitting procedure uses the sigmoidal function in Equation 1 to model mean bin number as a function of antigen concentration.
source: As illustrated in Figure 1E, this fitting procedure uses the sigmoidal function in Equation 1 to model mean bin number as a function of antigen concentration.
evidence: This is a description of the data analysis procedure.

claim: The need to account for multiple sources of noise in the Tite-Seq experiment necessitates a more complex inference procedure than Figure 1E might suggest.
source: However, the need to account for multiple sources of noise in the Tite-Seq experiment necessitates a more complex procedure than Figure 1E might suggest; the details of this inference procedure are described in Appendix 5.
evidence: This is a statement about the complexity of the data analysis.

claim: Each clone underwent the same labeling procedure as in the Tite-Seq experiment, after which median fluorescence values were measured using standard flow cytometry.
source: Each clone underwent the same labeling procedure as in the Tite-Seq experiment, after which median fluorescence values were measured using standard flow cytometry.
evidence: This is a description of the validation experiments.

claim: At least three replicate binding curves were measured for each clone in the validation experiments.
source: These curves, which can be directly compared to Tite-Seq measurements (Figure 4A), are plotted in Figure 4B; at least three replicate binding curves were measured for each clone.
evidence: This is a description of the validation experiments.

claim: The main discrepancy in error bar calculations occurred for clones c22 and c102.
source: The main discrepancy in these error bar calculations occurred for clones c22 and c102 (see also Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation from the data.

claim: The difference in fluorescein binding between OPT and WT scFvs at saturating concentrations was not due to variation in the total amount of displayed scFv.
source: This difference was not due to variation in the total amount of displayed scFv, which one might control for by labeling the c-Myc epitope as in Reich et al. (2015).
evidence: This is an inference from the data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 6.

claim: The difference in fluorescein binding between OPT and WT scFvs at saturating concentrations reflects a difference in the specific activity of displayed scFvs.
source: Rather, this difference in binding reflects a difference in the specific activity of displayed scFvs.
evidence: This is an inference from the data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 6.

claim: Yeast display experiments performed at a single antigen concentration cannot distinguish differences in specific activity from differences in scFv affinity.
source: Yeast display experiments performed at a single antigen concentration cannot distinguish such differences in specific activity from differences in scFv affinity.
evidence: This is an inference about the limitations of single-concentration experiments.

claim: In both the 1H and 3H variable regions, the large majority of mutations weaken antigen binding (1H: 88%; 3H: 93%).
source: In both regions, the large majority of mutations weaken antigen binding (1H: 88%; 3H: 93%), with many mutations increasing KD above our detection threshold of 10-5 M (1H: 36%; 3H: 52%).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Many mutations in the 1H and 3H variable regions increase KD above the detection threshold of 10^-5 M (1H: 36%; 3H: 52%).
source: In both regions, the large majority of mutations weaken antigen binding (1H: 88%; 3H: 93%), with many mutations increasing KD above our detection threshold of 10-5 M (1H: 36%; 3H: 52%).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Far fewer mutations in the 1H and 3H variable regions reduced KD (1H: 12%; 3H: 7%).
source: Far fewer mutations reduced KD (1H: 12%; 3H: 7%), and very few dropped KD below our detection limit of 10-9.5 M (1H: 0%; 3H: 3%).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Very few mutations in the 1H and 3H variable regions dropped KD below the detection limit of 10^-9.5 M (1H: 0%; 3H: 3%).
source: Far fewer mutations reduced KD (1H: 12%; 3H: 7%), and very few dropped KD below our detection limit of 10-9.5 M (1H: 0%; 3H: 3%).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Multiple random mutations in the 1H and 3H variable regions tend to further reduce affinity.
source: Histograms of the effect of two or three amino acid changes relative to WT, shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A, reveal that multiple random mutations tend to further reduce affinity.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Mutations within the 3H variable region have a larger effect on affinity than do mutations in the 1H variable region.
source: We also observed that mutations within the 3H variable region have a larger effect on affinity than do mutations in the 1H variable region.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Single amino acid mutations in 3H increased KD more than mutations in 1H (1H median KD = 10^-6.84; 3H median KD ≳ 10^-5.0; P = 4.7×10^-4, one-sided Mann-Whitney U test).
source: Specifically, single amino acid mutations in 3H were seen to increased KD more than mutations in 1H (1H median KD=10-6.84; 3H median KD≳10-5.0P=4.7×10-4; P=4.7×10−4, one-sided Mann-Whitney U test).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Binding affinity is more sensitive to variation in CDR3H than to variation in CDR1H.
source: This result suggests that binding affinity is more sensitive to variation in CDR3H than to variation in CDR1H, a finding that is consistent with the conventional understanding of these antibody CDR regions (Xu and Davis, 2000; Liberman et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an inference from the data, supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The 3H variable region appears to have a larger effect on scFv expression than the 1H variable region has.
source: These results suggest two things. First, the 3H variable region appears to have a larger effect on scFv expression than the 1H variable region has.
evidence: This is an inference from the data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The WT sequence appears to be more highly optimized for expression in CDR1H than in CDR3H.
source: At the same time, since we observe fewer beneficial mutations in 1H (Figure 5C) than in 3H (Figure 5D), the WT sequence appears to be more highly optimized for expression in CDR1H than in CDR3H.
evidence: This is an inference from the data shown in Figure 5C and 5D.

claim: The effect of double or triple mutations further reduced expression in both CDRs, similar to what was observed for affinity.
source: The effect of double or triple mutations further reduced expression in both CDRs (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B), similar to what was observed for affinity.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: A strong correlation was found between SK (sensitivity of affinity to mutations) and the number of contacts the WT residue makes within the protein structure.
source: To get a better understanding of what aspects of the structure might govern affinity, we plotted SK values against two other quantities: the number of amino acid contacts made by the WT residue within the antibody structure (Figure 6B), and the distance between the WT residue and the antigen (Figure 6C). We found a strong correlation between SK and the number of contacts, but no significant correlation between SK and distance to antigen.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: No significant correlation was found between SK (sensitivity of affinity to mutations) and distance to antigen.
source: We found a strong correlation between SK and the number of contacts, but no significant correlation between SK and distance to antigen.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: SE (sensitivity of expression to mutations) did not correlate significantly with either the number of contacts or distance to antigen.
source: By contrast, SE did not correlate significantly with either of these structural quantities (Figure 6D and E).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 6D and 6E.

claim: Tite-Seq provides a potentially powerful method for mapping the sequence-affinity trajectories of antibodies during the affinity maturation process.
source: Tite-Seq therefore provides a potentially powerful method for mapping the sequence-affinity trajectories of antibodies during the affinity maturation process, as well as for studying other aspects of the adaptive immune response.
evidence: This is a speculation about the potential applications of the method.

claim: The details of the Tite-Seq experiments (e.g., 11 antigen concentrations, four sorting bins per concentration, etc.) were chosen largely for experimental convenience.
source: The details of our Tite-Seq experiments (e.g., 11 antigen concentrations, four sorting bins per concentration, etc.) were chosen largely for experimental convenience.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental design choices.

claim: The effects of varying Tite-Seq parameters have not been systematically explored, and a future investigation of these effects might be valuable.
source: The effects of varying these parameters have not been systematically explored, and a future investigation of these effects might be valuable.
evidence: This is a speculation about future work.

claim: Simulations suggest that the primary source of noise in Tite-Seq experiments came not from a lack of sorted cells or Illumina reads, but rather from the inefficient post-sort recovery of antibody sequences.
source: These simulations, along with an analysis of synonymous variants (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), suggest that the primary source of noise in our experiments came not from a lack of sorted cells or Illumina reads, but rather from the inefficient post-sort recovery of antibody sequences.
evidence: This is an inference from the simulation results and analysis of synonymous variants.

claim: Improvements to the post-sort DNA recovery protocol might substantially improve the resolution of Tite-Seq.
source: We therefore suggest that improvements to our post-sort DNA recovery protocol might substantially improve the resolution of Tite-Seq.
evidence: This is a speculation about future improvements to the method.

claim: Tite-Seq fundamentally differs from prior DMS experiments in that full binding titration curves, not two-bin enrichment statistics, are used to determine binding affinities.
source: Tite-Seq fundamentally differs from prior DMS experiments in that full binding titration curves, not two-bin enrichment statistics, are used to determine binding affinities.
evidence: This is a statement about the key difference between Tite-Seq and previous methods.

claim: Protein sequence determines not just ligand-binding affinity, but also the quantity and specific activity of surface-displayed proteins.
source: The third advantage of measuring binding curves pertains to the fact that protein sequence determines not just ligand-binding affinity, but also the quantity and specific activity of surface-displayed proteins.
evidence: This is established knowledge in protein biochemistry.

claim: The data suggest that confounding effects of expression and specific activity can be large and can distort yeast display affinity measurements computed from enrichment statistics gathered at a single antigen concentration.
source: Our data (Figure 4—figure supplement 5 and Figure 4—figure supplement 6) suggest that these confounding effects can be large and that they can distort yeast display affinity measurements computed from enrichment statistics gathered at a single antigen concentration.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5 and Figure 4—figure supplement 6.

claim: Strong sequence-dependent effects on both the expression and specific activity of yeast-displayed proteins have been reported by other groups.
source: Strong sequence-dependent effects on both the expression and specific activity of yeast-displayed proteins has been reported by other groups as well (e.g., [Burns et al., 2014]), although the absence of such effects has also been reported (e.g., [Kowalsky and Whitehead, 2016]).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The magnitude of confounding effects of expression and specific activity is likely to vary substantially from protein to protein.
source: Ultimately, the magnitude of these effects is likely to vary substantially from protein to protein.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the variability observed in the literature.

claim: Many DMS studies using yeast display (e.g., epitope mapping studies) might not suffer from confounding effects of expression and specific activity, and in such cases it probably makes sense to employ a simpler experimental design than is required for Tite-Seq.
source: It should also be noted that many DMS studies using yeast display (e.g., epitope mapping studies [Kowalsky et al., 2015; Doolan and Colby, 2015; Van Blarcom et al., 2015]) might not suffer from these potentially confounding effects, and in such cases it probably makes sense to employ a simpler experimental design than is required for Tite-Seq.
evidence: This is a speculation about when simpler methods might be appropriate.

claim: Changing a protein's amino acid sequence can be expected to change multiple biochemical properties of that protein.
source: We wish to emphasize, more generally, that changing a protein's amino acid sequence can be expected to change multiple biochemical properties of that protein.
evidence: This is established knowledge in protein biochemistry.

claim: The work illustrates the importance of designing massively parallel assays that can disentangle the effects of sequence changes on multiple biochemical properties.
source: Our work illustrates the importance of designing massively parallel assays that can disentangle these effects.
evidence: This is an inference about the implications of the work.

claim: Tite-Seq provides a general solution to the problem of disentangling sequence effects on affinity from effects on expression and specific activity for massively parallel studies of protein-ligand binding.
source: Tite-Seq provides a general solution to this problem for massively parallel studies of protein-ligand binding.
evidence: This is a claim about the generalizability of the method.

claim: The Tite-Seq procedure can be readily applied to any protein binding assay that is compatible with yeast display and FACS.
source: Indeed, the Tite-Seq procedure described here can be readily applied to any protein binding assay that is compatible with yeast display and FACS.
evidence: This is a speculation about the generalizability of the method.

claim: Many protein binding assays compatible with yeast display and FACS have been developed.
source: Many such assays have been developed (Liu, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Tite-Seq can also be readily adapted for use with other expression platforms, such as mammalian cell display.
source: We expect that Tite-Seq can also be readily adapted for use with other expression platforms, such as mammalian cell display (Forsyth et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a speculation about the adaptability of the method, supported by a citation.

claim: As expected, variation in and around CDR3H had a larger effect on affinity than did variation in and around CDR1H.
source: As expected, we found that variation in and around CDR3H had a larger effect on affinity than did variation in and around CDR1H.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5.

claim: CDR1H is more optimized for protein expression than is CDR3H, an unexpected finding that appears to be novel.
source: We also found that CDR1H is more optimized for protein expression than is CDR3H, an unexpected finding that appears to be novel.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The finding that CDR1H is more optimized for expression than CDR3H suggests the possibility that secondary CDR regions might be evolutionarily optimized to help ensure antibody stability, thereby freeing up CDR3H to encode antigen specificity.
source: Still, this finding suggests the possibility that secondary CDR regions (such as CDR1H) might be evolutionarily optimized to help ensure antibody stability, thereby freeing up CDR3H to encode antigen specificity.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the data.

claim: If the hypothesis that secondary CDR regions are optimized for stability holds, it could provide a biochemical rationale for why CDR3H is more likely than CDR1H to be mutated in functioning receptors and why variation in CDR3H is often sufficient to establish antigen specificity.
source: If this hypothesis holds, it could provide a biochemical rationale for why CDR3H is more likely than CDR1H to be mutated in functioning receptors (Liberman et al., 2013) and why variation in CDR3H is often sufficient to establish antigen specificity (Xu and Davis, 2000).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the data, supported by citations.

claim: Tite-Seq can potentially shed light on the structural basis for antibody-antigen recognition.
source: Tite-Seq can also potentially shed light on the structural basis for antibody-antigen recognition.
evidence: This is supported by the structural analysis presented in Figure 6.

claim: A strong correlation was identified between the effect that a position has on affinity and the number of molecular contacts that the residue at that position makes within the antibody.
source: By comparing the effects of mutations with the known antibody-fluorescein co-crystal structure (Whitlow et al., 1995), we identified a strong correlation between the effect that a position has on affinity and the number of molecular contacts that the residue at that position makes within the antibody.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: No correlation of expression with the number of contacts was observed.
source: By contrast, no such correlation of expression with this number of contacts is observed.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: If the observation that affinity correlates with the number of contacts were to hold for other antibodies, it would suggest that the functional geometry of paratopes might be governed by networks of residues whose positions and orientations are strongly interdependent.
source: If our observation were to hold for other antibodies, however, it would suggest that the functional geometry of paratopes might be governed by networks of residues whose positions and orientations are strongly interdependent.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the data.

claim: The simple matrix model correctly predicts that OPT has higher affinity than WT.
source: Our simple model for the sequence affinity landscape of this scFv therefore correctly predicts that OPT has higher affinity than WT.
evidence: This is supported by the modeling results.

claim: The finding that only 4.7×10^-5 of random 6-mutation variants had affinity at or below the predicted OPT affinity is fully consistent with the fact that the mutations in OPT relative to WT were selected for increased affinity, providing additional confirmation of the validity of Tite-Seq measurements.
source: This finding is fully consistent with the fact that the mutations in OPT relative to WT were selected for increased affinity, an additional confirmation of the validity of our Tite-Seq measurements.
evidence: This is an inference from the simulation results.
